note: Registrations that render an authored `children` list while their registry meta
omits `isContainer`, so `validateTree` draws a FALSE `not-a-container` on a child
list the renderer then puts on the page. Measured on main@d06059f24 by
packages/components/src/renderers/__tests__/container-declaration-ratchet.test.tsx,
over the WHOLE registry at runtime -- 131 bare authoring tags of 293 registry keys;
58 render children, 13 declare the flag, 45 do not. 44 of those 45 are listed here
and `button` is the excluded 45th (see `excluded` below).
A RATCHET TO ZERO, NOT AN EXEMPTION LIST. objectui#6779's ruling admitted this
stock so the class could be closed today; every entry is debt that still has to be
paid. The pin is red in BOTH directions, which is what makes the list shrink-only:
- a tag that renders children, omits the flag and is NOT listed  -> red.
That is a NEW violation. Declare `isContainer` on the registration; do not
add a line here. Admitting an entry needs a ruling, the way these 44 got one.
- a listed tag that no longer violates                           -> red.
The defect is gone, so the entry is dead weight: delete the line. This is the
direction the list is supposed to move, and the red is how it gets noticed.
TO PAY ONE OFF: add `isContainer: true` to that registration's meta and delete its
line here. Do NOT instead stop the renderer from reading `schema.children` -- that
shrinks the check rather than paying the debt, and it would break authored pages.
Read the reasoning at packages/layout/src/index.ts (objectui#3900): `children` is a
BASE property of every node in the JSON protocol (`BASE_PROPS` in
sdui-parser/src/validate.ts), not a per-component authoring key, so the flag answers
the protocol question "does this node accept a child list?" and widens no spec
surface. A warning that LIES is worse than a missing one: it trains authors -- AI
authors especially -- to discount the TRUE `not-a-container` reports.
⚠️ CHECK THE PUBLIC TIER BEFORE PAYING ONE OFF. `renderers/layout/react-page.tsx`
builds the JSX scope of every `kind:'react'` page with
`if (!tag || cfg.isContainer) continue;` over `getPublicConfigs()`, so declaring the
flag on a PUBLIC tag also DELETES its injected identifier from every react page.
None of the 44 below is public (measured; the pin asserts it), so for them the
declaration provably removes nothing. `button` is the one that is -- which is why it
is excluded rather than listed.
`since` is the date the entry was admitted, so the list carries its own history: a
line dated later than this file's first commit was added after the ruling and needs
one of its own.

button.reason: Ruled out of this list by objectui#6779's maintainer ruling (2026-08-29), pending a separate card. It is the ONLY public-tier member of the 45, so declaring `isContainer` would delete `Button` from the JSX scope of every `kind:'react'` page -- and it reads `children` as a LABEL FALLBACK, not as layout containment, so the containment answer is a product decision rather than a mechanical fix. The pin asserts this entry still describes reality (renders children, undeclared, public): when the separate card lands, it goes red and this entry must be resolved rather than left standing.
